# HCL DX Compose · webinar runbook

> ℹ️ **Before you start: what this installer is, and what it is not**
>
> - **Built for:** Demo environments, tests, proofs of concept, training, and as a solid starting point for your own installation.
> - **Not a production sizing tool:** A production platform with high load expectations needs many tuning and adjustment values (JVM, pools, replicas, caches, storage, HA, security hardening) that are outside the scope of this tool.
> - **The most frequent options:** Its goal is not to cover every possible installation, but the most frequent ones, done right and tested.
> - **For large environments:** We recommend Professional Services to finish tuning the installation (on-site adjustments and custom parametrisation) or to customise the tool for your requirements.
> - **As is:** The software is provided as is, without warranty of any kind, under its MIT licence.
>

Generated by the DX Installer Wizard on 2026-11-10 08:39 UTC · https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com · installer v2.7.0-dev · Kubernetes · ingress-nginx (Ingress) · Helm 4

A tailor-made installation built from your answers. **This folder is self-contained**: every file is already filled in (values, properties, LDIF, secrets) and the commands run from this folder.

> ⚠️ **PoC, not production. Credentials in plain text:** passwords and keys are written in the files of this folder so that everything is easy to follow. Keep it private and rotate the secrets afterwards.

| | |
|---|---|
| `prepare.sh` | webinar phase 1: OpenLDAP and PostgreSQL (the rest is done live) |
| `demo.sh` | webinar phase 2: stages 0 to 5, one command at a time |
| `uninstall.sh` | deletes everything that was installed |
| `BUILD-INFO.txt` | what this folder was generated for (installer version, platform, Ingress, Helm, options): send it if something fails |
| `support/` | support data: environment-info.sh and the HCL collector (--collect) |
| `internals-ca/` | the CAs of corporate IT (directory and databases) that DX must trust |
| `prep-pki/` | plays the part of corporate IT: the keys of those CAs and the server certificates (preparation only) |

## Before you start

- You need `kubectl` (with access to the cluster), `helm`, `openssl`, `curl` and `python3`.
- **Helm 4:** the commands use `--wait=legacy` and `--force-conflicts`, which do not exist in Helm 3. With Helm 3, use `--wait` and leave out `--force-conflicts` (the scripts do it by themselves when they find Helm 3). `helm version` tells you which one you have.

## Resources this installation asks for

Kubernetes requests, measured on our lab cluster (DX Compose CF239).

| Part | What | CPU · memory |
|---|---|---|
| HCL software | DX Compose, HCL DX IQ, Search V2 (OpenSearch) | 7.7 CPU · 16 GiB |
| Prerequisites (third party) | OpenLDAP, PostgreSQL (CloudNativePG), LiteLLM | 0.4 CPU · 1.7 GiB |
| Extras and advanced tools | — | — |
| **Total** | | **8.1 CPU · 17.7 GiB** |

> The HCL requirement (~8 CPU, ~14 GiB) covers only the HCL software, **not** the prerequisites or the extras. Look for about **11 CPU · 24 GiB free** in the cluster (start-up peaks, restarts and the system pods).

## Phase 1 · Preparation (before the session)

Run it a day or a few hours before the webinar. It creates the namespace of the third-party tools and installs OpenLDAP and PostgreSQL, then stops: the environment is then ready for the session. The DX namespace and the sign-in to the HCL Harbor with the charts are done live in the demo, and LiteLLM at the start of stage 4, with IQ.

```bash
cd dx-install
./prepare.sh             # phase 1: OpenLDAP and PostgreSQL, then it stops
```

### Webinar preparation

#### P-1 · Check the cluster

```bash
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get storageclass dx-deploy-rwo dx-deploy-rwx
kubectl get ingressclass nginx || echo "IngressClass nginx not found (k3s creates traefik when it starts)"
```

#### P-2 · Namespace for the third-party tools

dx-shared: OpenLDAP and PostgreSQL now, LiteLLM in stage 4. The DX namespace, dx-demo, is created live in the demo.

```bash
kubectl apply -f lab-base/namespace-shared.yaml
```

#### P-3 · Corporate CAs (directory and databases): internals-ca/ and the server certificates

Plays the part of corporate IT: two root CAs, one for the directory and one for the databases, whose certificates stay in internals-ca/ (what IT would give you), and the server certificates of OpenLDAP and PostgreSQL signed by them (prep-pki/). Generated once: running it again keeps the files.

```bash
mkdir -p internals-ca prep-pki
[ -f prep-pki/corporate-directory-ca.key ] || openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:3072 -nodes -sha256 -days 3650 \
  -keyout prep-pki/corporate-directory-ca.key -out internals-ca/corporate-directory-ca.crt -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=Corporate IT/CN=EUROPESIP Corporate Directory Root CA"
[ -f prep-pki/corporate-database-ca.key ] || openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:3072 -nodes -sha256 -days 3650 \
  -keyout prep-pki/corporate-database-ca.key -out internals-ca/corporate-database-ca.crt -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=Corporate IT/CN=EUROPESIP Corporate Database Root CA"
[ -f prep-pki/openldap.crt ] || { openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout prep-pki/openldap.key -out prep-pki/openldap.csr \
  -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=Corporate IT/CN=openldap.dx-shared.svc.cluster.local" && \
  openssl x509 -req -in prep-pki/openldap.csr -CA internals-ca/corporate-directory-ca.crt -CAkey prep-pki/corporate-directory-ca.key -CAcreateserial -sha256 -days 825 \
  -extfile prep-pki/openldap.ext -out prep-pki/openldap.crt; }
[ -f prep-pki/postgres.crt ] || { openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout prep-pki/postgres.key -out prep-pki/postgres.csr \
  -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=Corporate IT/CN=dx-pg-rw.dx-shared.svc.cluster.local" && \
  openssl x509 -req -in prep-pki/postgres.csr -CA internals-ca/corporate-database-ca.crt -CAkey prep-pki/corporate-database-ca.key -CAcreateserial -sha256 -days 825 \
  -extfile prep-pki/postgres.ext -out prep-pki/postgres.crt; }
kubectl -n dx-shared create secret generic openldap-tls --type=kubernetes.io/tls --from-file=tls.crt=prep-pki/openldap.crt \
  --from-file=tls.key=prep-pki/openldap.key --from-file=ca.crt=internals-ca/corporate-directory-ca.crt --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n dx-shared create secret generic dx-corporate-directory-ca --from-file=ca.crt=internals-ca/corporate-directory-ca.crt --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n dx-shared create secret tls dx-pg-tls --cert=prep-pki/postgres.crt --key=prep-pki/postgres.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n dx-shared create secret generic dx-pg-corporate-ca --from-file=ca.crt=internals-ca/corporate-database-ca.crt --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

#### P-4 · OpenLDAP with the demo users

The LDIF already carries the users with {SSHA} hashed passwords.

```bash
kubectl apply -f lab-ldap/secrets.openldap.yaml
kubectl -n dx-shared create configmap openldap-demo-ldif --from-file=00-demo-users.ldif=lab-ldap/demo-users.ldif --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
helm repo add helm-openldap https://jp-gouin.github.io/helm-openldap/
helm upgrade --install openldap helm-openldap/openldap-stack-ha --version 4.3.3 -n dx-shared \
  -f lab-ldap/openldap-values.yaml --wait=legacy --timeout 10m
```

#### P-5 · Check groups and members (optional)

*Optional check.*

```bash
kubectl -n dx-shared exec openldap-0 -c openldap-stack-ha -- \
  env LDAPTLS_CACERT=/opt/bitnami/openldap/certs/ca.crt ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldaps://localhost:1636 -D cn=admin,dc=dxdemo,dc=com -w '<REDACTED>' -b ou=groups,dc=dxdemo,dc=com cn uniqueMember
```

#### P-6 · PostgreSQL 18: CloudNativePG operator, users and cluster

dx_core is prepared by your setup-postgres-dx.sql when the cluster is created.

```bash
helm repo add cnpg https://cloudnative-pg.github.io/charts
helm upgrade --install cnpg cnpg/cloudnative-pg --version 0.29.1 -n dx-shared --wait=legacy --timeout 10m
kubectl apply -f lab-bbdd/secrets.yaml
kubectl -n dx-shared create configmap dx-pg-setup-sql --from-file=lab-bbdd/setup-postgres-dx.sql --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -     # your table creation script
kubectl apply -f lab-bbdd/cluster-dx-pg.yaml
kubectl -n dx-shared wait clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io/dx-pg --for=condition=Ready --timeout=10m
```

> ✅ When `prepare.sh` finishes, the environment is **ready for the session**: stop there and continue on the day of the demo.

## Phase 2 · The demo (the day of the webinar)

`demo.sh` shows each command and waits for **Enter** before running it (s = skip, q = quit). It runs the checks too.

> **Imperative or declarative.** There are two usual ways to create Kubernetes objects such as secrets: imperative, with commands like `kubectl create secret`, and declarative, describing them in YAML files applied with `kubectl apply`. GitOps works with the declarative one, so it is the one this webinar follows.

```bash
./demo.sh                # phase 2: stages 0 to 5, one command at a time
./demo.sh --from 3-1      # resume from a step
./demo.sh --no-pause      # without stopping before each step
./uninstall.sh           # after the webinar: delete everything
```

### 0 · Prerequisites

📖 HCL documentation: [DX Compose · Preparation](https://help.hcl-software.com/digital-experience/dx-compose/CF239/deploy_dx/install/kubernetes_deployment/preparation/)

#### 0-1 · Check that the environment is ready

What the preparation left ready: the cluster and, in dx-shared, OpenLDAP and PostgreSQL.

```bash
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get storageclass dx-deploy-rwo dx-deploy-rwx
kubectl -n dx-shared get pods                      # OpenLDAP and PostgreSQL: Running
kubectl -n dx-shared get clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io   # dx-pg: Cluster in healthy state
```

#### 0-2 · Namespace for DX: dx-demo

Two versions of the same namespace: the generic one, for any Kubernetes, and the OpenShift one, with the annotations HCL requires for the restricted-v2 SCC.

```bash
cat lab-base/namespace-dx.yaml              # any Kubernetes
cat lab-base/namespace-dx.openshift.yaml    # OpenShift
kubectl apply -f lab-base/namespace-dx.yaml
```

### 1 · Base DX installation

📖 HCL documentation: [DX Compose · Installation](https://help.hcl-software.com/digital-experience/dx-compose/CF239/deploy_dx/install/kubernetes_deployment/install/)

#### 1-1 · Secrets

Pull secret (lab-base/secret-harbor.yaml), the Helm charts (signing in to hclcr.io with the same encrypted file) and wpsadmin (lab-base/secrets.yaml) + a self-signed TLS certificate for HAProxy. There are two usual ways to create Kubernetes objects such as these secrets: imperative, with commands like kubectl create secret, and declarative, describing them in YAML files applied with kubectl apply. GitOps works with the declarative one, so it is the one this webinar follows (the TLS secret is built from the certificate files).

```bash
# The two secrets of the base are in Git encrypted with SOPS: names readable, values ENC[AES256_GCM,...]
cat lab-base/secret-harbor.yaml
# Pull secret: decrypted on the fly and applied; the clear value never touches the disk
sops -d lab-base/secret-harbor.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# The same encrypted file gives Helm the Harbor password, through stdin: then the charts of DX, IQ and Search
sops -d --extract '["stringData"][".dockerconfigjson"]' lab-base/secret-harbor.yaml \
  | jq -r '.auths["hclcr.io"].password' \
  | helm registry login hclcr.io -u 'andres@europesip.com' --password-stdin
mkdir -p charts
helm pull oci://hclcr.io/dx-compose/hcl-dx-deployment --version 2.50.0 -d charts
helm pull oci://hclcr.io/dx/hcl-dx-iq --version 1.0.3 -d charts
helm pull oci://hclcr.io/dx-compose/hcl-dx-search --version 2.37.0 -d charts
# wpsadmin: decrypted in place, so it stays in clear text for the rest of the labs, then applied
sops -d -i lab-base/secrets.yaml
kubectl apply -f lab-base/secrets.yaml
[ -f lab-base/dx-tls.crt ] || openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -sha256 -days 365 -keyout lab-base/dx-tls.key -out lab-base/dx-tls.crt \
  -subj "/CN=dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com"
kubectl -n dx-demo create secret tls dx-tls-cert --cert=lab-base/dx-tls.crt --key=lab-base/dx-tls.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

> 🔐 **SOPS in this step.** Both files are encrypted with [SOPS](https://github.com/getsops/sops) and an
> [age](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age) key, as they would be in a Git repository: `.sops.yaml` says which files and
> fields are encrypted, and for which public key. You need `sops`, `age`, `jq` and the private key in
> `~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt`. Two ways to use them: `sops -d file | kubectl apply -f -` decrypts on the fly (the pull
> secret, and `sops -d --extract` for the Harbor password that Helm reads from stdin), and `sops -d -i file` decrypts the file in place (wpsadmin), which then must **not** be pushed to Git again
> (`sops -e -i file` encrypts it back). The rest of the labs use plain YAML files.

#### 1-2 · Install DX Compose (15-25 min the first time)

In another terminal: kubectl -n dx-demo get pods -w.

```bash
helm upgrade --install dx-deployment charts/hcl-dx-deployment-2.50.0.tgz -n dx-demo \
  -f lab-base/custom-values.yaml \
  --timeout 30m --wait=legacy
```

#### 1-3 · Check DX with kubectl port-forward (before the Ingress)

Most installation problems come from the particularities of the network (DNS, firewall, load balancer, the ports of the workstation). kubectl port-forward opens a tunnel, through the Kubernetes API, from a port of your workstation to the HAProxy Service of DX: no Ingress, no DNS and no open ports. If DX answers here and later fails through the Ingress, the problem is in the route or the network, not in DX.

```bash
kubectl -n dx-demo port-forward svc/dx-deployment-haproxy 8443:443 >/dev/null 2>&1 & PF=$!; sleep 5   # a tunnel: localhost:8443 -> HAProxy of DX
curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'https://localhost:8443/wps/portal -> HTTP %{http_code}\n' https://localhost:8443/wps/portal || true
kill $PF
```

#### 1-4 · External access

```bash
kubectl apply -f lab-base/ingress-dx.yaml
```

#### 1-5 · Check the portal (optional)

*Optional check.*

```bash
kubectl -n dx-demo get pods
for i in $(seq 1 30); do c=$(curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com/wps/portal); [ "$c" != 404 ] && [ "$c" != 000 ] && break; sleep 5; done
echo "https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com/wps/portal -> HTTP $c"
```

### 2 · LDAP configuration

📖 HCL documentation: [DX Compose · LDAP configuration](https://help.hcl-software.com/digital-experience/dx-compose/CF239/deploy_dx/manage/cfg_webengine/ldap_configuration/)

#### 2-1 · Connect DX to the LDAP (~5 min)

OpenLDAP is already installed (external dependencies): this adds the LDAP layer to DX.

```bash
kubectl apply -f lab-ldap/secrets.yaml     # the bind secret dx-ldap-bind (dx-demo)
helm upgrade --install dx-deployment charts/hcl-dx-deployment-2.50.0.tgz -n dx-demo \
  -f lab-base/custom-values.yaml \
  -f lab-ldap/custom-values.ldap-basic.yaml \
  --timeout 30m --wait=legacy
```

> **Manual step:** Give the **Administrator** role to the `dxadmins` group: portal as wpsadmin → *Administration → Access → Resource Permissions → Virtual Resources → PORTAL*.

#### 2-2 · Administrator role for the group dxadmins (XMLAccess)

XMLAccess is the configuration interface of DX: this request gives the Administrator role, on the virtual resource PORTAL, to the LDAP group dxadmins. The same can be done in the Resource Permissions page.

```bash
WPS_PW=$(kubectl -n dx-demo get secret web-engine-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d)
curl -sk -u "wpsadmin:$WPS_PW" -H 'Content-Type: text/xml' --data-binary @lab-ldap/admin-role.xml \
  https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com/wps/config | grep -o '<status[^>]*>'
```

#### 2-3 · Configuration overrides: sign in by e-mail, preferred language and LDAPS (~5 min)

The complete LDAP layer replaces the basic one: overrides (loginProperty mail, preferredLanguage), port 636 with SSL, and the corporate CAs of internals-ca/ in the truststore of Liberty. The database CA will validate PostgreSQL over SSL in stage 3.

```bash
kubectl -n dx-demo create secret generic dx-corporate-cas --from-file=internals-ca/corporate-directory-ca.crt --from-file=internals-ca/corporate-database-ca.crt \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -     # the corporate CAs, for the truststore of Liberty
helm upgrade --install dx-deployment charts/hcl-dx-deployment-2.50.0.tgz -n dx-demo \
  -f lab-base/custom-values.yaml \
  -f lab-ldap/custom-values.ldap.yaml \
  --timeout 30m --wait=legacy
```

#### 2-4 · Only LDAPS: close plain LDAP in OpenLDAP

DX already uses LDAPS: OpenLDAP now requires TLS for every connection, and plain LDAP (389) is rejected.

```bash
kubectl -n dx-shared exec openldap-0 -c openldap-stack-ha -- \
  ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://localhost:1389 -D cn=admin,dc=dxdemo,dc=com -w '<REDACTED>' -b dc=dxdemo,dc=com -s base dn     # plain LDAP: it still works
printf 'dn: cn=config\nchangetype: modify\nreplace: olcSecurity\nolcSecurity: tls=1\n' | \
  kubectl -n dx-shared exec -i openldap-0 -c openldap-stack-ha -- ldapmodify -Q -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:///
kubectl -n dx-shared exec openldap-0 -c openldap-stack-ha -- \
  ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://localhost:1389 -D cn=admin,dc=dxdemo,dc=com -w '<REDACTED>' -b dc=dxdemo,dc=com -s base dn \
  || echo "Plain LDAP rejected: TLS is required (DX keeps working over LDAPS)"
```

📖 HCL documentation: [HCL DX IQ · Installation](https://help.hcl-software.com/digital-experience/9.5/CF239/build_sites/iq/installation/) · [HCL DX IQ · Deploying LiteLLM](https://help.hcl-software.com/digital-experience/9.5/CF239/build_sites/iq/installation/deploy-litellm/)

*Optional check.*

```bash

curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"iq-general-purpose","max_tokens":1000,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Answer only: ready"}]}'; echo
```

```bash

  -f lab-ldap/custom-values.ldap.yaml \
  -f lab-bbdd/custom-values.postgres.yaml \
```

#### 4-5 · Ask IQ from the terminal (optional)

*Optional check.*

```bash
curl -sk -c cookies.txt -o /dev/null -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"username":"wpsadmin","password":"<REDACTED>"}' https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com/dx/api/core/v1/auth/login
```

### 5 · Search

📖 HCL documentation: [DX Compose · Enabling search](https://help.hcl-software.com/digital-experience/dx-compose/CF239/deploy_dx/manage/cfg_dx_compose/enable_search/)

#### 5-1 · OpenSearch certificates: a CA for the lab

Mutual TLS between OpenSearch and the Search Middleware: first a small certificate authority that signs the three certificates.

```bash
mkdir -p lab-search/certs && cd lab-search/certs
printf 'basicConstraints = CA:FALSE\nkeyUsage = digitalSignature, keyEncipherment\nextendedKeyUsage = serverAuth, clientAuth\n' > ext.cnf
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -sha256 -days 730 -keyout root-ca-key.pem -out root-ca.pem \
  -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=DX Compose Labs/CN=dx-search-root-ca"
cd ../..
```

#### 5-2 · OpenSearch certificates: admin

Its subject (CN=admin) is the adminDN of the search values.

```bash
cd lab-search/certs
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout admin-key.pem -out admin.csr \
  -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=DX Compose Labs/CN=admin"
openssl x509 -req -in admin.csr -CA root-ca.pem -CAkey root-ca-key.pem -CAcreateserial -sha256 -days 730 \
  -extfile ext.cnf -out admin.pem
cd ../..
```

#### 5-3 · OpenSearch certificates: node

For the OpenSearch nodes, between themselves.

```bash
cd lab-search/certs
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout node-key.pem -out node.csr \
  -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=DX Compose Labs/CN=opensearch-node"
openssl x509 -req -in node.csr -CA root-ca.pem -CAkey root-ca-key.pem -CAcreateserial -sha256 -days 730 \
  -extfile ext.cnf -out node.pem
cd ../..
```

#### 5-4 · OpenSearch certificates: client

For the Search Middleware towards OpenSearch.

```bash
cd lab-search/certs
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout client-key.pem -out client.csr \
  -subj "/C=ES/O=EUROPESIP/OU=DX Compose Labs/CN=opensearch-client"
openssl x509 -req -in client.csr -CA root-ca.pem -CAkey root-ca-key.pem -CAcreateserial -sha256 -days 730 \
  -extfile ext.cnf -out client.pem
cd ../..
```

#### 5-5 · One secret per certificate

Each one with its certificate, its key and the CA.

```bash
kubectl -n dx-demo create secret generic search-admin-cert \
  --from-file=lab-search/certs/admin.pem --from-file=lab-search/certs/admin-key.pem --from-file=lab-search/certs/root-ca.pem \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n dx-demo create secret generic search-node-cert \
  --from-file=lab-search/certs/node.pem --from-file=lab-search/certs/node-key.pem --from-file=lab-search/certs/root-ca.pem \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n dx-demo create secret generic search-client-cert \
  --from-file=lab-search/certs/client.pem --from-file=lab-search/certs/client-key.pem --from-file=lab-search/certs/root-ca.pem \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

#### 5-6 · Install hcl-dx-search (OpenSearch + Search Middleware)

```bash
helm upgrade --install dx-search charts/hcl-dx-search-2.37.0.tgz -n dx-demo \
  -f lab-search/custom-search-values.yaml \
  --timeout 20m --wait=legacy
```

#### 5-7 · Enable Search V2 in DX (~5 min)

```bash
helm upgrade --install dx-deployment charts/hcl-dx-deployment-2.50.0.tgz -n dx-demo \
  -f lab-base/custom-values.yaml \
  -f lab-ldap/custom-values.ldap.yaml \
  -f lab-bbdd/custom-values.postgres.yaml \
  -f lab-iq/custom-values.iq.yaml \
  -f lab-search/custom-values.search.yaml \
  --timeout 30m --wait=legacy
```

#### 5-8 · Check the search API (optional)

*Optional check.*

```bash
curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com/dx/api/search/v2/explorer/ -> HTTP %{http_code}\n' https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com/dx/api/search/v2/explorer/
```

## Done

Portal: https://dx-demo.apps.promox.europesip-lab.com/wps/portal (wpsadmin / your lab password).

## If something fails

- Fix the cause and resume from the step that failed: `./demo.sh --from <step>`.
- **Frequent errors** (Helm 3, ports 80/443 with k3s in WSL, nip.io names…): https://github.com/europesip/hcl-dx-compose-installer/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md
- **To ask for help**, send:
  - `BUILD-INFO.txt`: what this folder was generated for (installer version, platform, Ingress, Helm and options). It has no secrets.
  - `support/environment-info.sh > environment-info.txt`: your workstation, the tools, the cluster, the Ingress and the access to DX.
  - Or everything at once: `./demo.sh --collect` makes the `.tar.gz` that HCL Support asks for, with both files above and the secrets masked. Review it before sending it.
